categories.name: Overall
categories.description: Broad language-model performance across the current LiveBench release.
categories.methodology: Equal-weight mean of all 7 category means, matching the published aggregation method for complete results. This is LiveBench performance, not a universal best-model score.

categories.name: Reasoning
categories.description: Logical, spatial and multi-step reasoning tasks.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 4 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Coding
categories.description: Code generation and completion on the published LiveBench tasks.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 2 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Agentic coding
categories.description: JavaScript, TypeScript and Python agentic coding tasks.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 3 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Mathematics
categories.description: Competition mathematics, symbolic work and problem solving.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 4 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Data analysis
categories.description: Working with tables and structured information.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 3 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Language
categories.description: Language puzzles, connections and text understanding.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 3 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Instructions
categories.description: Following constraints in rewriting, summaries and generation.
categories.methodology: Arithmetic mean of the 4 published task scores in this category. Only complete results are ranked. Exact model and effort configurations are preserved.

categories.name: Capability index
categories.description: One general-capability score that combines results from many benchmarks. Higher is better. The scale has no fixed maximum, so compare models rather than reading it as a percentage.
categories.methodology: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) as published by Epoch AI, with its published confidence interval. It is a statistical combination of many benchmarks, not a single test.

categories.name: GPQA Diamond
categories.description: Graduate-level multiple-choice questions in biology, chemistry and physics, written by experts to be hard to answer with a web search. Random guessing scores 25%.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: Mock AIME 2024–2025
categories.description: Competition mathematics in the style of the AIME exam, from the OTIS olympiad program. Every answer is a whole number from 0 to 999.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

rows.provider: Allen Institute for AI,University of Washington

categories.name: FrontierMath Tiers 1–3
categories.description: Original, unpublished mathematics problems from advanced undergraduate to research level, written by mathematicians and checked automatically.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: FrontierMath Tier 4
categories.description: The hardest FrontierMath set: exceptionally difficult research-level problems.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: MATH Level 5
categories.description: The hardest level of the MATH competition problem set. Leading models now score near the top, so it separates older and smaller models best.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

rows.provider: Allen Institute for AI,University of Washington

categories.name: SWE-bench Verified
categories.description: Real issues from open-source Python projects. The model must change the code so the project’s tests pass. Engineers confirmed each task is solvable.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: SimpleQA Verified
categories.description: Short factual questions with a single correct answer, testing whether a model recalls facts accurately.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: Chess puzzles
categories.description: Chess puzzles given to the model as text, scored on finding the correct moves.
categories.methodology: Best published score for each exact model configuration, as evaluated by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort used. Standard errors are shown where the source reports them.

categories.name: DeepSWE
categories.description: Original, long software engineering tasks from active open-source projects in TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust. Every model runs in the same minimal agent, mini-swe-agent.
categories.methodology: Pass@1 averaged over repeated runs, with average API cost, output tokens and agent steps per task, as published by Datacurve and compiled by Epoch AI. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort. Standard errors are derived from the published 95% intervals.

categories.name: CursorBench
categories.description: Ambiguous, multi-file coding tasks drawn from real sessions in the Cursor editor, run and scored by Cursor.
categories.methodology: Scores, average cost, tokens and steps per task as published by Cursor and compiled by Epoch AI. Cost applies list prices per million tokens to each model’s token use. A suffix such as _high names the reasoning effort.

categories.name: SWE-bench Verified, bash only
categories.description: The 500 SWE-bench Verified issues from real Python projects, with every model in the same minimal agent that can only run shell commands (mini-SWE-agent).
categories.methodology: Share of issues resolved, with average API cost and model calls per issue, as published by the SWE-bench team. The latest run of each model and reasoning effort is kept; a suffix such as _high names the effort.

categories.name: Image generation
categories.description: Text-to-image composition and visual reasoning, evaluated by T2I-CoReBench.
categories.methodology: Published overall scores with the Gemini 2.5 Flash evaluator. These measure composition and reasoning across 12 dimensions, not human aesthetic preference. Prompt-rewriting variants and other evaluators are excluded. Coverage is limited to models evaluated by the source.

categories.name: Arena text
categories.description: People ask two anonymous models their own question and vote for the better answer. The ranking comes from millions of these blind votes.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena WebDev
categories.description: People describe a web page or app; two anonymous models each build it, and people vote for the better working result.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published WebDev scores. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena coding
categories.description: Blind votes on conversations about code: people compare two anonymous answers to their own programming question.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena math
categories.description: Blind votes on the math questions people asked two anonymous models.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena hard prompts
categories.description: Blind votes on the hardest prompts: complex, specific questions that need real problem solving.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena creative writing
categories.description: Blind votes on the stories, poems and other writing people asked for.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.

categories.name: Arena instruction following
categories.description: Blind votes on prompts with specific instructions, judged on how well each answer follows them.
categories.methodology: Arena’s published scores with style control, which separates what an answer says from its length and formatting, as Arena’s leaderboard shows by default. Higher is better on an open-ended scale, like chess ratings; the range is Arena’s 95% confidence interval.
